source.title: Stochastic Kernel Regularisation Improves Generalisation in Deep Kernel Machines
source.authors: Edward Milsom; Ben Anson; Laurence Aitchison

record.tranche_reason: Compares test performance for neural networks trained with Adam-family optimizers and SGD, using a different set of architectures and recipes than the optimizer studies named in V4.
record.gate_note: Only the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 neural-network Adam/SGD comparisons test V4. The DKM regularization ablations, condition-number measurements, and comparisons to prior kernel methods do not test the listed versions. Other relevant findings are listed under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam/AdamW versus momentum-SGD held-out results for wide ResNet20-inspired classifiers on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, bearing on V4 in these recipes. It is not an original source. Different schedules and weight decay prevent attributing the differences solely to optimizer choice; the tuning budget is unspecified.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the main interpretation: SKR and numerical-stability improvements enabling faster, longer training raise DKM CIFAR-10 accuracy to 94.52%, supporting the importance of representation learning in kernel methods. The DKM matches the Adam network's accuracy but trails the SGD network on both datasets. SGD's poorer DKM stability is a brief observation, not a held-out generalization result.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares Adam or AdamW with SGD on same-architecture image classifiers trained for 1200 epochs, but optimizer settings, schedules, and weight decay differ. The paper's main intervention is stochastic kernel regularization for a deep kernel machine, not an optimizer study.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (CIFAR-10 versus CIFAR-100); optimizer recipes and weight-decay/scheduler settings differ.

fits_no_version.finding: SKR improves the convolutional DKM's CIFAR-10 accuracy: 94.52% with the full method versus 93.71% without SKR, with differing numerical-failure rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stochastic regularization of learned Gram matrices can improve held-out accuracy in convolutional deep kernel machines.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger SKR slows worsening Gram-matrix conditioning in a toy DKM, but condition numbers converge with sufficiently long training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SKR can delay deterioration of learned Gram-matrix conditioning without changing its eventual value in this toy setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Brief DKM experiments found SGD generally less stable than Adam, without reporting a held-out optimizer comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects numerical stability in deep kernel machines.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison uses different optimizer-specific hyperparameter recipes and does not report matched training performance, so the test-performance gap cannot be isolated from those recipe differences. CIFAR-100 optimizer settings are incompletely stated. Results use 4 random seeds and report 1 standard error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V4 optimizer-comparison rows were reported separately beyond the two metrics for each dataset. DKM results and ablations were excluded from rows because they do not measure an optimizer comparison named by the versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected neural-network performance and the contribution of local connectivity.

Matched training performance; a documented limited versus broader tuning budget; language tasks; switching optimizers; and a controlled coupled versus decoupled weight-decay comparison. The AdamW result alone does not test whether decoupling recovers performance.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Neural-network dropout effects, small-data regimes, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with alternative generalization measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: R1/R2, R3/R4, R5/R6, and R7/R8 each present the same contrast in opposite directions; they are not independent replications. All table values match the supplied text. Recipe differences qualify causal interpretation but do not themselves establish a limits_scope verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label evaluation.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected network comparison.

Does not compare optimizer performance across language tasks or report training performance. It compares a limited set of image-classification recipes; the Adam and SGD learning-rate schedules and weight-decay settings differ.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch batch-size study.
Does not test dropout in neural networks; stochastic kernel regularization is a different intervention on deep kernel machines.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: Neural Network (Adam)
rows.size_stated: network widths {512, 1024, 2048} in the three blocks; comparable number of parameters to the convolutional deep kernel machine
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; initial learning rate 0.001 and the same learning-rate scheduling as the convolutional deep kernel machine.

conditions.value: ResNet20-inspired; same architecture as the DKM

rows.note: The Adam model's test accuracy is slightly lower than the SGD model's; the paper reports no significant difference between the Adam neural network and the DKM, but does report a p-value of 0.0001 comparing the DKM with the SGD network.
rows.check: Change partial to observed: Adam accuracy is 94.55% versus SGD's 95.36%. V4 specifies worse held-out performance without a minimum gap. The reported significance tests compare the DKM with neural networks, not Adam directly with SGD.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, ResNet20-inspired network, 1200 epochs, reported Adam and momentum-SGD recipes
relationships.reason: R1–R4 show Adam below SGD in accuracy (94.55% versus 95.36%) and log-likelihood (−1.3003 versus −0.2112); schedules and weight decay differ, and tuning scope is unspecified.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam accuracy and log-likelihood trail momentum SGD, but the comparisons remain unverified and schedules and weight decay differ.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100, same-architecture neural networks, reported AdamW and SGD-with-weight-decay recipes
relationships.reason: R5–R8 show AdamW below SGD in accuracy (74.13% versus 79.42%) and log-likelihood (−1.9183 versus −0.8890), despite adding weight decay and cosine scheduling; optimizer settings are incompletely documented.
relationships.display_finding: Reported AdamW accuracy and log-likelihood trail SGD, but the comparisons remain unverified and optimizer settings are incompletely documented.
